question: On contrast-enhanced CT, signs of bowel ischaemia in a strangulated hernia include bowel wall thickening, absence of mucosal enhancement, mesenteric fat stranding, and free fluid — collectively indicating compromised viability requiring urgent surgery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. CECT findings of bowel ischaemia — thickened wall, absent mucosal enhancement, fat stranding, and free fluid — are the imaging correlates of strangulation and predict the need for bowel resection at emergency surgery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. These CT features are the radiological correlates of ischaemia: wall thickening and loss of enhancement reflect mural ischaemia; mesenteric fat stranding indicates congestion and inflammation; free fluid suggests third-space loss or perforation. Their presence confirms the need for emergency surgery and resection of non-viable bowel.
